title: Processed assignment unchanged where the restriction stays free
statement: Fix $n$, and let $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ be restrictions on $n$ variables. Run the clause-processing procedure on a list of literals (each paired with its position index) together with a decision-tree path, starting from $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$, and write $\rho_0'$ and $\sigma'$ for the two restrictions it returns. If a variable $v$ is free under the input, $\rho_0(v) = \mathrm{none}$, and remains free under the output, $\rho_0'(v) = \mathrm{none}$, then the procedure has not altered $\sigma$ at $v$ either: $\sigma'(v) = \sigma(v)$.
hypotheses_covered: v is free under the input restriction ($\rho_0(v) = \mathrm{none}$)
v remains free under the output restriction ($\rho_0'(v) = \mathrm{none}$)
replaced:
If $\rho_0\,v = \mathrm{none}$ and \texttt{SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits} leaves
$\rho_0$ unset at $v$, then it also leaves $\sigma$ unchanged at $v$; the $\sigma$ output
equals the input $\sigma$ at $v$, since $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ are updated at the same
variables in lockstep.
